purpose: Consistent concept targets and native-image gap evaluation; no runtime implementation.
sharedDirection:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: a coherent production art-direction reference set for the original VECTOR RUSH / NOCTURNE anti-gravity racing game. This is generated concept art, never evidence of an implemented game.
STYLE LOCK FOR ALL FOUR IMAGES: carefully authored, credible premium real-time game art; solid constructible industrial transit infrastructure; restrained surface detail that survives the ordinary chase camera. Charcoal graphite road and metal, blue-slate concrete, pearl ceramic craft, black glazing, small citron paint accents, cool-white practical lamps, sparse cyan guidance, localized warm amber interiors. Night, blue-gray atmospheric distance, readable middle values in near architecture, dark intervals between light pools. Three clear depth layers. Structure is visible through broad illumination and ambient occlusion, not just glowing contours. Keep scene readable with normal camera exposure, modest bloom, no cinematic bokeh or motion blur.
ROAD LOCK: dark satin composite with a few irregular damp patches and fine believable expansion joints. Broad broken elongated practical-light highlights tied to visible light sources. Preserve large dark aggregate areas; no mirror flood, puddle carpet, glitter, diagonal polygon bands, or dense decorative lane graphics.
CRAFT LOCK: faithfully preserve the provided native Kestrel 07 silhouette, proportions, geometry arrangement and paint placement: two parallel long pearl-white armored nacelles with waists and top recessed intakes; a narrow low glossy-black central canopy/graphite keel; visible dark gaps and short mounting connections; two large recessed circular rear engine mouths plus one TINY central nozzle. No fins, wings, wheels, extra engines, fatter armor, elongated tails or redesigned fuselage. Flush black 07 marking on the same left rear nacelle, three short black bars on the other, small citron accents. Improve finish through pearl/graphite/glass/metal distinction, restrained seams, edge thickness, contact shading and existing form's specular roll. Engine light stays inside deep throats with small pale cores, dim thin cyan rims, short soft translucent cyan exhaust and restrained local spill. Never a giant glowing ring, solid cone or opaque blue puddle.
CONSISTENCY: every view belongs to this same craft and circuit, with the same finish, exposure philosophy, fixture family and architecture. No franchise logos, billboards, new gameplay features or new HUD. Do not use an illustrated mock interface.

IMAGE A — OPENING CITY BEND / MASTER LOOK.
INPUT 1 is the actual native opening bend: composition, road elevation/width/curve/bank, horizon, camera pose, craft position and projected size, signal-mast location and overall paired-upright silhouette are authoritative.
INPUT 2 is the actual native craft neutral rear-quarter view: geometry identity reference only, not a request for its studio camera or lighting.
Create ONE landscape 16:9 frame, preferably 1920x1080. Render a finished target of precisely this passage. Retain the native banked chase perspective and craft at about its current 20 percent frame width in the lower center. Keep its road bend and cross-track spans; the landmark with two unequal uprights and one offset occupied room stays at its native location. Keep the racing line open.
Improve the existing city's construction and connection: articulate the existing near track fascia and supports with a service ledge and recessed fixtures, join the middle building bases with a limited connected podium/service-street layer, use a small number of substantial differentiated building volumes, and quiet the far skyline with grouped low-contrast windows and atmospheric depth. Avoid a suddenly much denser city or oversized new landmarks. The paired signal mast reads as a built assembly with braces, panel thickness and restrained occupied-room light. Existing overhead lamps create broad readable road/material response; surrounding near architecture receives soft visible light.
Remove all original HUD overlays, including the map and counters, but change neither the scene framing nor the craft's scale to fill that space. No opponents absent from this native view. No labels or text except existing 07 and small original craft marks. The goal is a measurable whole-frame appearance target, with source-related light, a connected city and the existing playable-space composition.

IMAGE B — AMBER GALLERY / SAME GAME, SAME CRAFT, SAME MATERIALS.
INPUT 1 is the current native amber-gallery screenshot and is the composition authority. Retain its exact left-curving route, road width/elevation/bank, near wall and ceiling rib positions, exit aperture, tilted horizon, ordinary racing camera, and projected craft size/position. The existing service hatch remains part of the wall.
INPUT 2 is the new opening-city MASTER LOOK: use its exact craft identity and surface palette, lamp/rail family, road material character and overall polish. Do not bring its exterior composition into this image.
Create ONE landscape 16:9 frame. Translate the established master look to this actual enclosed passage. Refine existing shell into believable thick chamfered structural ribs, recessed metal cassettes, service-wall panels and an integrated hatch. Make geometry legible through light falloff and contact shading. Existing amber fixtures illuminate nearby ceiling/wall returns, producing rhythmic warm road highlights with dark intervals. Use a satin/damp road matching the master with large dark areas; do not turn the corridor into a copper mirror or add dozens of lamps. Warm light gently changes the same pearl craft without altering white armor to gold. Maintain the compact engine throat/core/exhaust configuration from the master. Frame the same blue-hazed city through the clear existing exit. Restrain cyan to thin guidance and recessed lamps.
Remove the original HUD only. No extra vehicles, renamed craft, new logo, title, labels, camera repositioning, new tunnel length or enlarged craft. Favor material/lighting/structural finishing of the native forms over replacing the gallery design.

Existing broad lights wrap cylinders rather than washing them all flat. Add only details explaining the existing asset's construction; do not invent refinery stacks, steam, giant signs, new silos, excessive greebles or a different landmark.
